title: Bordure - Cycling management game
author: Xalfenouille
selftext:
Hello,

Let me introduce **Bordure**, my current side-project.

I've loved management games for years, especially sports management such as Football Manager or Pro Cycling Manager. But in  PCM, most of the time you're micro-managing every attack and every effort of every rider. I wanted the opposite, closer to Football Manager or OOTP: you're the directeur sportif. You build the season, prepare the team and write the race plan. Then you follow the race from the car, radio in hand. The riders make the decisions. You steer them.

![img](gz2x4n2ogaxh1 "Launch screen")

![img](owaja1u9pdxh1 "Choosing a team")

It's a solo, offline desktop game. I've been working on it for a while, and it's finally at a point where I'd like to show it. I'm not into 3D and fancy stuff while playing management games. I'm dying for Football Manager 2D engine over 3D boring stuff. That's why I conceived the game with the idea in mind that we're following a live feed event with timings, elevation, events, etc.

![img](buwfxldygaxh1 "In race: Live feed")

**The rule I won't break: you give intentions, never watts, never micro managing.**

You never pick a power output, a trajectory or the exact moment of an attack. You set a team plan before the start (objectives, roles, missions by phase of the race). During the race you send radio orders to specific riders, like "cover the break" or "protect the leader until the foot of the climb", with an end condition.

* Orders take time to arrive and need an acknowledgement. You can track who received what.
* Riders interpret orders according to their character. Sometimes they simply can't carry them out.
* Repeating an order gives no bonus. Spamming the radio doesn't work.
* You can also do nothing. A race finishes sensibly with just your plan.

![img](4xwt2nr4haxh1 "Establish your gameplan before the race")

**The AI plays by the same rules as you**

Rival teams use the same plans, the same rules and the same perception as your team. Nothing is scripted. If a break wins, it's because it worked. Races have crosswinds and echelons, rain, cobbles and gravel, time trials and full Grand Tours. A flat race and a mountain stage are different problems.

**You only know what your car knows**

The UI never shows the engine's real state. It shows projections with a source and an age. An event appears in the feed only if one of your riders saw it or it's public (finish line, abandons, race-radio announcements). Gaps are estimates and weather is what the car sees. Your picture of the race can be out of date, and that matters.

![img](hke6pkfchaxh1 "Race finish and debriefs")

**Under the hood**

* Speed physics (gradient, aero, drafting) and two energy reserves, explosive efforts and endurance. Groups and gaps emerge from the simulation. They aren't scripted.
* A fitness-fatigue training model with annual planning by blocks, altitude camps and recovery debt. Overtrain a rider and they get hurt.
* Fully deterministic: same seed + same content + same commands = same result. I rely on this to calibrate the sim statistically against real race outcomes.
* Presentation never affects the sim. Watching at x1 or x64, with or without pauses, gives the identical race.

**Beyond race day**

* Career: a multi-season loop with a season calendar, A/B/C priorities from sponsor objectives, gear, finances and sponsors.
* Squad and progression: riders have 15 attributes, hidden dispositions and a living file. Power tests reveal real numbers, and staff give assessments rather than certainties.
* Market and contracts: negotiate live with agents. Riders have their own wants and a patience limit. Retirements and new pros come through each year.
* Draft mode: found your own team, then every team (including the AI ones) picks riders in turn from the whole pool. 
* National teams and Worlds, national championships, UCI calendar.
* Moddable content: teams, riders and courses are fully modable, so the game can supports community databases. A real-world 2026 pack is in the works. There's also an editor with GPX import.
* English (AI translated, not native, so expect wonky translations?) and French.

![img](vyy44m1ghaxh1 "Squad overview")

![img](cprbcraihaxh1 "Rider details")

**About the development**

It's TypeScript with Electron and React because web is what I'm most familiar with. The simulation engine has no UI or system-clock dependencies, so it runs the same in tests, in the CLI and in the app. Most of the work has gone into the sim and the AI rather than the interface. I'd like to be upfront that the project is AI-assisted (well we are on r/aigamedev so): I orchestrate, specify and review, and Claude writes much of the code. Each feature/PR/iteration goes through a strict loop of incremental reviews depending on the sensitivity of the ticket (which has got most of the engine issues). I'll send validate content through playthrough and testing loops.

I've been having a lot of fun working on/orchestrating this project. I've implemented a small CI/CD to test/validate code produced and actually learned a lot (even though I haven't produced most of the codebase).

Windows/Mac packages available, though only really tested on MacOS.

Demo/alpha is available on [itch.io](https://xalfen.itch.io/bordure)   
Game details are available on [bordure-game.com](https://bordure-game.com/en/) 

Hope you'll enjoy it as much as I do :) .
